passages.text: “Man, who is born of woman, is short of days and full of trouble.
passages.sermon: Man is born of a woman.\r\nMan lives only a short time.\r\nMan experiences much trouble.
passages.original: אָ֭דָם יְל֣וּד אִשָּׁ֑ה קְצַ֥ר יָ֝מִ֗ים וּֽשְׂבַֽע־ רֹֽגֶז׃

passages.text: Like a flower, he comes forth, then withers away; like a fleeting shadow, he does not endure.
passages.sermon:
Man is born from a woman.
He is like a flower.
He comes out and grows for a short time.
He soon withers and dies.
He is like a shadow that quickly passes by.
He does not last.
He cannot remain.
passages.original: כְּצִ֣יץ יָ֭צָא וַיִּמָּ֑ל וַיִּבְרַ֥ח כַּ֝צֵּ֗ל וְלֹ֣א יַעֲמֽוֹד׃

passages.text: Do You open Your eyes to one like this? Will You bring him into judgment before You?
passages.sermon:
God, You see man.
Man is born of woman.
Man lives a short life.
Man’s life is full of trouble.
You look at such a person.
You bring this person into judgment with You.
passages.original: אַף־ עַל־ זֶ֭ה פָּקַ֣חְתָּ עֵינֶ֑ךָ וְאֹ֘תִ֤י תָבִ֖יא בְמִשְׁפָּ֣ט עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Who can bring out clean from unclean? No one!
passages.sermon:
No one can make something clean from what is unclean.
No person can do this.
Only God is holy and pure.
People cannot create purity from impurity.
No one has this power.
passages.original: מִֽי־ יִתֵּ֣ן טָ֭הוֹר מִטָּמֵ֗א לֹ֣א אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: Since his days are determined and the number of his months is with You, and since You have set limits that he cannot exceed, look away from him and let him rest, so he can enjoy his day as a hired hand.
passages.sermon:
God determines each person’s life.
God knows the number of months each person will live.
God sets limits for every person’s life.
No one can go beyond these limits.
God, turn Your attention away from the person.
Let the person rest.
Let him enjoy his day like a hired worker.
passages.original: אִ֥ם חֲרוּצִ֨ים׀ יָמָ֗יו מִֽסְפַּר־ חֳדָשָׁ֥יו אִתָּ֑ךְ חֻקּוֹ עָ֝שִׂ֗יתָ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲבֽוֹר׃ שְׁעֵ֣ה מֵעָלָ֣יו וְיֶחְדָּ֑ל עַד־ יִ֝רְצֶ֗ה כְּשָׂכִ֥יר יוֹמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For there is hope for a tree: If it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its tender shoots will not fail.
passages.sermon:
A tree can have hope.
If someone cuts down the tree, it can grow again.
The tree will send out new shoots.
Its tender shoots will not stop growing.
passages.original: כִּ֤י יֵ֥שׁ לָעֵ֗ץ תִּ֫קְוָ֥ה אִֽם־ יִ֭כָּרֵת וְע֣וֹד יַחֲלִ֑יף וְ֝יֹֽנַקְתּ֗וֹ לֹ֣א תֶחְדָּֽל׃

passages.text: If its roots grow old in the ground and its stump dies in the soil, at the scent of water it will bud and put forth twigs like a sapling.
passages.sermon:
A tree can have old roots in the ground.
Its stump can die in the soil.
But water can change this.
When the tree smells water, it will bud.
It will grow new shoots.
It will put out branches like a young plant.
passages.original: אִם־ יַזְקִ֣ין בָּאָ֣רֶץ שָׁרְשׁ֑וֹ וּ֝בֶעָפָ֗ר יָמ֥וּת גִּזְעֽוֹ׃ מֵרֵ֣יחַ מַ֣יִם יַפְרִ֑חַ וְעָשָׂ֖ה קָצִ֣יר כְּמוֹ־ נָֽטַע׃

passages.text: But a man dies and is laid low; he breathes his last, and where is he?
passages.sermon:
A man dies.
He becomes weak.
A person breathes his last.
No one knows where he is.
passages.original: וְגֶ֣בֶר יָ֭מוּת וַֽיֶּחֱלָ֑שׁ וַיִּגְוַ֖ע אָדָ֣ם וְאַיּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: As water disappears from the sea and a river becomes parched and dry, so a man lies down and does not rise. Until the heavens are no more, he will not be awakened or roused from sleep.
passages.sermon:
Water can disappear from the sea.
A river can dry up and become parched.
A man can lie down in death.
He does not rise again.
He will not wake up.
He will not be roused from his sleep.
This will last until the heavens are no more.
passages.original: אָֽזְלוּ־ מַ֭יִם מִנִּי־ יָ֑ם וְ֝נָהָ֗ר יֶחֱרַ֥ב וְיָבֵֽשׁ׃ וְאִ֥ישׁ שָׁכַ֗ב וְֽלֹא־ יָ֫ק֥וּם עַד־ בִּלְתִּ֣י שָׁ֭מַיִם לֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ וְלֹֽא־ יֵ֝עֹ֗רוּ מִשְּׁנָתָֽם׃

passages.text: If only You would hide me in Sheol and conceal me until Your anger has passed! If only You would appoint a time for me and then remember me!
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job suffers greatly.
Job wishes for relief from his suffering.
Job says, "If only You would hide me in Sheol."
Sheol is the place of the dead.
Job asks God to conceal him there.
Job wants God to hide him until God's anger passes.
Job asks God to set a time for him.
Job wants God to remember him after that time.
passages.original: מִ֤י יִתֵּ֨ן׀ בִּשְׁא֬וֹל תַּצְפִּנֵ֗נִי תַּ֭סְתִּירֵנִי עַד־ שׁ֣וּב אַפֶּ֑ךָ תָּ֤שִׁ֥ית לִ֖י חֹ֣ק וְתִזְכְּרֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: When a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait, until my renewal comes.
passages.sermon:
A man can die.
Will this man live again?
I work hard all my days.
I wait with hope through my struggle.
I wait until my renewal comes.
passages.original: אִם־ יָמ֥וּת גֶּ֗בֶר הֲיִ֫חְיֶ֥ה כָּל־ יְמֵ֣י צְבָאִ֣י אֲיַחֵ֑ל עַד־ בּ֝֗וֹא חֲלִיפָתִֽי׃

passages.text: You will call, and I will answer; You will desire the work of Your hands.
passages.sermon:
God, You are the Creator.
You made me with Your own hands.
You will call to me.
I will answer You.
You will long for the work You have made.
passages.original: תִּ֭קְרָא וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֶֽעֱנֶ֑ךָּ לְֽמַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יָדֶ֣יךָ תִכְסֹֽף׃

passages.text: For then You would count my steps, but would not keep track of my sin.
passages.sermon: God, You would count my steps.\r\nYou would not keep track of my sin.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ עַ֭תָּה צְעָדַ֣י תִּסְפּ֑וֹר לֹֽא־ תִ֝שְׁמ֗וֹר עַל־ חַטָּאתִֽי׃

passages.text: My transgression would be sealed in a bag, and You would cover over my iniquity.
passages.sermon:
God is the subject.
God deals with my sin.
God seals my transgression in a bag.
God covers over my iniquity.
passages.original: חָתֻ֣ם בִּצְר֣וֹר פִּשְׁעִ֑י וַ֝תִּטְפֹּ֗ל עַל־ עֲוֺנִֽי׃

passages.text: But as a mountain erodes and crumbles and a rock is dislodged from its place, as water wears away the stones and torrents wash away the soil, so You destroy a man’s hope.
passages.sermon:
A mountain can fall down.
A mountain can crumble.
A rock can move from its place.
Water can wear away stones.
Floods can wash away the soil from the earth.
God destroys the hope of a man.
passages.original: וְ֭אוּלָם הַר־ נוֹפֵ֣ל יִבּ֑וֹל וְ֝צ֗וּר יֶעְתַּ֥ק מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ׃ אֲבָנִ֤ים׀ שָׁ֥חֲקוּ מַ֗יִם תִּשְׁטֹֽף־ סְפִיחֶ֥יהָ עֲפַר־ אָ֑רֶץ וְתִקְוַ֖ת אֱנ֣וֹשׁ הֶאֱבַֽדְתָּ׃

passages.text: You forever overpower him, and he passes on; You change his countenance and send him away.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power over a man forever.
God causes the man to go away.
God changes the man’s face.
God sends the man away.
passages.original: תִּתְקְפֵ֣הוּ לָ֭נֶצַח וַֽיַּהֲלֹ֑ךְ מְשַׁנֶּ֥ה פָ֝נָ֗יו וַֽתְּשַׁלְּחֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: If his sons receive honor, he does not know it; if they are brought low, he is unaware.
passages.sermon:
A man dies.
His sons may become honored.
He does not know it.
His sons may suffer shame.
He does not understand it.
He is unaware of what happens to his children after his death.
passages.original: יִכְבְּד֣וּ בָ֭נָיו וְלֹ֣א יֵדָ֑ע וְ֝יִצְעֲר֗וּ וְֽלֹא־ יָבִ֥ין לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: He feels only the pain of his own body and mourns only for himself.”
passages.sermon:
A man suffers pain in his own body.
He feels this pain personally.
He mourns only for himself.
He grieves for his own soul.
He does not notice the pain or honor of others.
He remains focused on his own suffering.
passages.original: אַךְ־ בְּ֭שָׂרוֹ עָלָ֣יו יִכְאָ֑ב וְ֝נַפְשׁ֗וֹ עָלָ֥יו תֶּאֱבָֽל׃פ
